task: Initial context setup, AGENTS.md and BMAD specification
prompt: I have an AI in SDLC assignment. I need to add approval limits by role to an invoice approval service in Java Spring Boot. Rules: Manager may approve up to $50,000; Director may approve up to $500,000; Above $500,000 needs two distinct approvers, second must be Director; Same user cannot count as both approvers; Failed attempt leaves invoice unchanged with a clear reason. Build the project in invoice-approval/ directory. Start by writing AGENTS.md so any AI agent arriving cold understands the domain, then produce a BMAD specification and task breakdown.
ai_actions: Detected Java 17 and Maven 3.9 from environment
Created invoice-approval/AGENTS.md with approval rules table, package layout, demo credentials, test command, 10 required scenarios, review expectations
Created invoice-approval/docs/spec/approval-limits-spec.md with BMAD format: Goal, Actors, Business Rules B1-B3, Acceptance Criteria AC-1 to AC-11
Created invoice-approval/docs/spec/task-breakdown.md with T-1 to T-10 task list mapped to git commit strategy
human_intervention: Reviewed AGENTS.md and added explicit instruction: 'identity check must fire BEFORE role check for dual-approver path' — this was missing from agent's first draft
Reviewed spec: added AC-7b explicitly testing error message wording to distinguish identity-before-role ordering
notes: Agent initially produced spec without the identity-before-role ordering constraint. Human review caught this and added it as a dedicated acceptance criterion AC-7b.

task: Step 1 — single-approver limits (Manager ≤50k, Director ≤500k) with unit tests
prompt: Implement Step 1 only: single-approver limits. Manager can approve invoices <= $50,000. Director can approve invoices <= $500,000. Use a pure domain class ApprovalService with no Spring annotations. Inject InvoiceRepository as a constructor parameter. Add JUnit 5 unit tests for every rule: exact limits, one dollar over, Manager/Director exact boundary. Do NOT implement the dual-approver rule yet — just throw a clear exception for amounts above Director limit.
follow_up_prompts: The test for managerApproveAtExactLimit should also assert the invoice status is APPROVED after success, not just that no exception was thrown
Add a test that verifies the invoice status is still PENDING_APPROVAL after a rejected attempt — the clean-fail guarantee is a key requirement
external_tools: mvn test (run after generation to verify)
ai_actions: Created ApprovalLimits.java with MANAGER_LIMIT=50000, DIRECTOR_LIMIT=500000, hasManagerAuthority(), hasDirectorAuthority() helpers
Created Invoice.java entity with id, vendorName, amount, status, firstApprover, firstApproverRole, decidedAt, decisionNote fields
Created InvoiceStatus.java enum: DRAFT, PENDING_APPROVAL, APPROVED, REJECTED
Created InvoiceRepository.java interface: findById, save, update
Created ApprovalRuleException.java and InvoiceNotFoundException.java
Created ApprovalService.java with approve() method: Manager branch (<=50k), Director branch (<=500k), high-value stub
Created FakeInvoiceRepository.java test double
Created initial 8 unit tests covering scenarios 1-5
human_intervention: Added follow-up prompt to assert invoice status after success (agent only checked no exception was thrown)
Added follow-up prompt to add clean-fail test (agent did not include this in first draft)
Manually verified test names matched the 10 required scenarios in AGENTS.md
notes: Agent's first draft did not include the clean-fail guarantee test. Two follow-up prompts were required. Commit a2103e7 includes only step-1 files so it is independently verifiable.

prompt: Now implement the dual-approver rule for invoices above $500,000. Requirements: first approval by any Director sets firstApprover field and leaves invoice PENDING; same user as firstApprover is blocked — identity check must fire BEFORE role check so the error message says 'same person' not 'you need Director role'; second approver must be a Director; second distinct Director finalises approval to APPROVED. Add JUnit 5 tests for scenarios 6-10: first Director approval, same-Director block, non-Director second-approver block, identity-before-role ordering test, successful dual-approval.
follow_up_prompts: The identityCheckFiresBeforeRoleCheck test is checking the exception message — make it assert the message contains 'same person' or 'different person', not just that an exception is thrown
Add an explicit test where a Manager attempts to be the second approver — this should fail with a role error, not an identity error
ai_actions: Extended ApprovalService.java: added approveHighValue() private method
Implemented identity guard: if (approverUsername.equals(invoice.getFirstApprover())) throw with 'must be from a different person'
Implemented role guard: if (!hasDirectorAuthority(approverRole)) throw with 'second approver must be a Director'
Identity check ordered BEFORE role check — verified by test 7b
Added 19 more unit tests: scenarios 6-10 plus edge cases
Total test count: 27 tests
human_intervention: Follow-up prompt #1: tightened the identityCheckFiresBeforeRoleCheck test to assert the actual message wording
Manually read ApprovalService.approveHighValue() to verify the if-statement ordering — identity check is line 89, role check is line 95
notes: The ordering of identity-before-role was flagged in AGENTS.md as a known agent failure mode. The agent did implement it correctly, but the test was too weak (checked exception type only). Human intervention strengthened the test to check message content.

task: REST API layer, session auth, static UI
prompt: Wire up the Spring Boot REST API. Create: AuthController with POST /api/auth/login and /logout using hardcoded demo users (no @Value injection — keep it simple); SessionStore backed by ConcurrentHashMap<String,UserSession>; SessionAuthFilter extending OncePerRequestFilter that reads Authorization bearer token and attaches UserSession to request attribute; ApprovalsController that reads username and role from session attribute and delegates to ApprovalService; InvoicesController with list, create, submit endpoints; InfrastructureConfig that wires InMemoryInvoiceRepository as InvoiceRepository bean and registers ApprovalService as a bean with @Service removed from the domain class; static HTML/JS/CSS UI seeded with test invoices INV-1001 through INV-1007 covering all test scenarios; application.properties on port 8080.
follow_up_prompts: The AuthController has an unused @Value parameter — remove it, credentials should come from the DemoUser inner class only
Move @Service off ApprovalService domain class — domain should have no Spring dependency. Wire it in InfrastructureConfig instead
ai_actions: Created InvoiceAppApplication.java with @SpringBootApplication
Created AuthController.java: DemoUser inner class with 4 hardcoded users (demo.manager/MANAGER, demo.director/DIRECTOR, demo.director2/DIRECTOR, demo.admin/ADMIN); login returns 200+token or 401
Created SessionStore.java: ConcurrentHashMap, createSession(), getSession(), removeSession()
Created SessionAuthFilter.java: reads Authorization header, skips /api/auth/**, attaches UserSession to request attribute 'user'
Created ApprovalsController.java: POST /api/approvals/{id}/approve delegates to approvalService.approve(); POST /api/approvals/{id}/reject
Created InvoicesController.java: GET /api/invoices, POST /api/invoices, POST /api/invoices/{id}/submit
Created InMemoryInvoiceRepository.java seeded with 7 invoices at various amounts
Created InfrastructureConfig.java: @Bean ApprovalService, @Bean InvoiceRepository
Created index.html, app.js, styles.css
human_intervention: Finding #1: AuthController had @Value("${demo.users}") injected but ignored — agent included it unnecessarily. Human caught this in code review and prompted removal
Finding #5: ApprovalService had @Service annotation from domain layer — violates layering rule. Human caught this and prompted move to InfrastructureConfig
Manually tested login with curl before recording demo
notes: Two PR findings required human-prompted fixes: @Value removal and @Service migration. Both were caught by human code review before commit, not by the agent proactively.

prompt: Write Playwright E2E tests for the invoice approval UI at http://localhost:8080. Use TypeScript. Write exactly 5 tests: (1) Manager approval of invoice INV-1006 ($75,000) is rejected — assert error message contains '50000' and invoice status remains PENDING_APPROVAL; (2) Director first approval of INV-1007 ($750,000) — assert invoice stays pending after single Director approval; (3) Same Director blocked as second approver on INV-1007 — assert error says 'different person'; (4) Manager blocked as second approver — assert error mentions role; (5) Manager can reject an over-limit invoice with a reason — reject should always work regardless of amount.
follow_up_prompts: The playwright.config.ts should set baseURL to http://localhost:8080 and use a single chromium project only
Test 1 must also navigate to the Invoices tab AFTER the rejection and assert the status cell still shows PENDING — the clean-fail guarantee must be verified end-to-end

Created invoice-approval/e2e/playwright.config.ts with baseURL http://localhost:8080, chromium only, 2 retries
Created invoice-approval/e2e/tests/approval-limits.spec.ts with 5 tests
Test 1 navigates to Invoices tab after rejection and asserts PENDING_APPROVAL in status cell
human_intervention: Follow-up prompt #1: added baseURL and single-project config
Follow-up prompt #2: test 1 initially did not navigate back to verify invoice status — human caught this was a key assignment requirement and added the check
Manually reviewed each test selector against the actual UI HTML to verify locators would match
notes: Critical gap in test 1: agent did not include the post-rejection status check. Human reviewer caught it. This is exactly the kind of 'looks right and is not' issue the assignment warns about.

task: PIT mutation testing and PR review with verdicts
prompt: Run PIT mutation testing and report the score. Then run a PR review against the full diff. For every finding, assign one of three verdicts: fixed, dismissed with reason, or deferred with reason. Output the review in a structured table.
follow_up_prompts: For each surviving mutation, explain WHY it survived and whether it represents a real gap or an acceptable survivor
Update ASSIGNMENT.md with the mutation scores (before and after) and the PR review findings table
ai_actions: Ran PIT mutation coverage — 57 mutations generated, 50 killed (88%), line coverage 92%
Analysed 7 surviving mutations: 5 VoidMethodCallMutator (setDecidedAt, setDecisionNote, setFirstApprover audit setters), 2 no-coverage mutations in unseeded code paths
Produced PR review with 5 findings
Produced structured verdict table
Updated ASSIGNMENT.md with scores and table
human_intervention: Reviewed each surviving mutation individually and confirmed 5 audit-field survivors are acceptable (no business logic)
Made final verdict decisions: findings 1 and 5 Fixed, findings 2 and 3 Dismissed, finding 4 Deferred
Verified ASSIGNMENT.md write-up is accurate before committing
notes: PIT ran successfully. Mutation score of 88% is acceptable: NegateConditionalsMutator 100%, ConditionalsBoundaryMutator 100%. All business-logic mutations are killed. Survivors are audit/logging setters with no business logic consequence.

pr_review_findings.finding: AuthController injects @Value("${demo.users}") but field is never read — dead parameter
pr_review_findings.action: Removed @Value parameter; credentials defined in DemoUser inner class

pr_review_findings.finding: InvoicesController.submit() does not verify who is submitting — any authenticated user can submit any draft
pr_review_findings.reason: Demo application scope; real implementation would add ownership check

pr_review_findings.finding: FakeInvoiceRepository.update() is a no-op — tests rely on same object reference
pr_review_findings.reason: Tests mutate the same Invoice object reference; no copy is made so mutations are immediately visible. Documented in FakeInvoiceRepository.

pr_review_findings.finding: E2E tests share mutable in-memory state — test 4 depends on test 3 having run first
pr_review_findings.reason: A beforeEach API endpoint to reset seeded invoices would fix this. Out of scope for demo assignment.

pr_review_findings.finding: @Service on ApprovalService violates domain-layer purity — domain package should have no Spring dependency
pr_review_findings.action: Moved @Bean declaration to InfrastructureConfig; removed @Service from ApprovalService.java
